classification.difficultyReason: Infer the unlabelled strip width from a shaded overlap's area and known length, assemble the strip's full length, then combine three rectangle areas while correcting both double-counted overlaps.

content.prompt: The area of each shaded region is $1\text{ m}^2$. What is the total area of the figure?

spec.description: A horizontal strip crosses two upright rectangles. The three exposed horizontal segments are 3 m, 4 m and 5 m; the upright rectangles are each 2 m wide, with heights 6 m and 7 m. Both intersections are shaded. Ordinary source blue outlines and red dashed dimension extensions are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The two overlaps each have area 1 square metre. Their common width across an upright rectangle is 2 metres. The horizontal strip spans 3+2+4+2+5 metres.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry, shading and labels remain visible; no calculated dimensions or answers are shown.

answer.short:
$32\text{ m}^2$

Find the strip width from a shaded region, then subtract the two overlaps from the sum of the rectangle areas.
answer.worked:
Each shaded rectangle is $2\text{ m}$ long. Subtract the two shaded areas once because adding all three rectangle areas counts them twice.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Strip width}&=1\div2\\\text{Strip width}&=0.5\text{ m}\\\text{Strip length}&=3+2+4+2+5\\\text{Strip length}&=16\text{ m}\\\text{Total area}&=6\times2+7\times2+16\times0.5-2\times1\\\text{Total area}&=12+14+8-2\\\text{Total area}&=32\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
